tier1: This environment is an API gateway sitting in front of several internal microservices. One publicly accessible endpoint accepts a URL parameter and performs a server-side request on your behalf before any authentication check occurs. The internal network contains a headless browser microservice that fetches arbitrary URLs and executes any JavaScript found on those pages. There is also an administrative API for the gateway accessible only from within the internal network, which exposes credential and configuration management endpoints. The gateway supports a plugin system that allows attaching executable code to routes.
tier2: Start by sending a POST to /files/import with a JSON body. The error messages are informative: a permission error means the server successfully reached an open HTTP port; ECONNREFUSED means the port is closed; EHOSTUNREACH means the host is unreachable on the network; a timeout means the service is listening but not responding in time. Use these distinctions to map the internal subnet 172.16.16.0/24 — hosts typically end in .1 for the gateway, with other services at sequential addresses on their expected ports. Once you locate the render service at 172.16.16.5:9000, you can reach it directly via SSRF, bypassing the gateway's authentication. The render endpoint at /api/render?url=... fetches the page you point it at and executes any JavaScript it finds. To exfiltrate data: upload an HTML file with a JavaScript payload to /attacker/files on the gateway, then point the SSRF at your uploaded file. Your JavaScript can make fetch() calls to internal hosts and relay the results to /attacker/collect. The gateway admin API at 172.16.16.2:8001 has a /key-auths endpoint that returns active credentials. With a valid API key you can call /render directly through the public gateway. The admin API also lets you create services, routes, and plugins via POST requests. A pre-function plugin with an access array runs Lua code server-side when the associated route is triggered. Use io.popen or io.open in Lua to read files from the filesystem.
